Seminar Title:

Valorization of Cottonseed Byproducts and Development of an Eco-Friendly Protein based Bio-nanocomposite Film

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Food Process Engineering

Speaker Name:

Kishore Kumar G ( Rollno : 523fp1004)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

CH-113

Date and Time:

14 Oct 2026 11:00 AM

Contact:

Sushil Kumar Singh

Abstract:

The increased usage of plastics for food packaging applications causes pollution, greenhouse gas emissions, and waste accumulation, which are global concerns. This has captured the attention of researchers to develop biodegradable packaging material as an alternative to plastic materials. Agro-plant wastes are a potential resource for biopolymers like protein and polysaccharides. Cottonseed cake and hulls are the byproducts of cottonseed oil industries. They are often used as animal feed and fertilizers. They contain protein biopolymers and cellulose as their major constituents that can be used to produce biodegradable packaging materials. However, these biopolymer-based packaging materials inherently lag in certain properties, such as heat resistance, gas barrier properties, and mechanical strength. Hence, reinforcing materials should be added to increase their strength and structural properties. In this research, zinc oxide nanoparticles have been green-synthesized using cottonseed cake extract, and nanocrystalline cellulose has been extracted from cottonseed hulls via an ultrasound-enhanced acid hydrolysis process. Different synthesis conditions, such as room temperature, high temperature (65 &degC), and ultrasound treatment (50 % amp, 30 min), and different cottonseed cake extract concentrations (45, 60, and 75 % (v/v)) were evaluated for nanoparticle synthesis and desired particle properties. The UV spectroscopy, XRD, and FESEM characterization studies confirmed the formation of the ZnO structure at an average particle size of 60 nm. Also, the synthesized nanoparticles have exhibited antioxidant and antimicrobial properties. The protein has been extracted from cottonseed cake, and the functional properties have been enhanced by cold plasma treatment (10 &ndash 30 kV, 10 &ndash 30 min) to enhance their film-forming ability for packaging applications. The treatment produced significant alterations in the particle size, zeta potential, functional properties, and oxidation characteristics. However, the effect of cold plasma on gossypol content is redistribution rather than detoxification. Cellulose nanocrystals have been extracted at different acid concentrations (50 and 60 % (v/v)) and ultrasound power (30 % and 50 %). The synthesis conditions significantly affected the particle size and structural properties. This modified protein biopolymer, zinc oxide nanoparticles, and cellulose nanocrystals will be used to develop eco-friendly nanocomposite materials. Hence, the developed bio-nanocomposite will have the antimicrobial, mechanical strength, and barrier properties needed for packaging materials. Also, the cottonseed byproducts will be efficiently utilized to promote waste valorization and foster a sustainable circular bioeconomy.
